summary: Historical recovery of the completed 11 November evening report. All five source story topics are retained as concise, independently checked summaries. This is not a current market snapshot.
limitations: The original report had targeted, partial Reuters coverage; earlier uncovered intervals remain unresolved.
Original article dates are verified, but separate initial-publication and update times are not established. Date-only sources do not establish exact intraday timing.
Historical observations and proposed terms apply to the source cutoff, not the date this recovery was published.
Cross-report duplicate checks cover the retained public editions and accessible source responses, not all inaccessible briefing history.

sources.title: Alphabet eyes $3 billion Hong Kong, Singapore bond sale, sources say
EU threatens significant fines for unfair online trade practices
China's central bank vows to step up policy support for the economy
After US market shake-out, signs suggest too soon to say worst is over
Japan advisers urge focus on sustaining growth after inflation hits BOJ goal

stories.headline: Alphabet explores SGD and HKD borrowing
stories.body: Reuters cited sources saying Alphabet sought about US$3 billion from inaugural SGD and HKD issues. Proposed minimums were S$1.5 billion and HK$8 billion; SGD maturities could extend to 30 years. Final size, timing and pricing were unsettled at the report cutoff.
stories.analysis: Long maturity adds rate sensitivity; proposed borrowing is not a completed issuance.
stories.watch_next: Final terms, pricing, size and settlement.

stories.headline: EU proposes stronger online consumer rules
stories.body: Reuters described a proposed Digital Fairness Act and a separate consumer-protection enforcement revision allowing fines up to 6% of global annual revenue. The proposals still needed legislative agreement; this was not an enacted fine or a penalty already imposed.
stories.analysis: Platforms may face additional compliance costs if the proposals become law.
stories.watch_next: Final legislative scope and enforcement provisions.

stories.headline: PBoC reiterates monetary support
stories.body: Reuters reported that the PBoC's quarterly policy report pledged counter-cyclical support, stronger domestic demand, low overall borrowing costs and a broadly stable yuan. These were policy commitments, not a newly quantified rate cut or liquidity injection.
stories.analysis: Policy direction alone does not establish immediate currency or funding-market effects.
stories.watch_next: Specific policy actions and domestic demand.

stories.headline: Tech positioning signals remain mixed
stories.body: Reuters analysis cited Deutsche Bank data showing technology positioning below April 2025 lows and Carrick Lane evidence of reduced AI call-option buying. Other technical indicators remained cautious; the reporting did not establish that the selloff had ended.
stories.analysis: Reduced crowding can help stabilisation without proving a durable market bottom.
stories.watch_next: Options flows, market breadth and company cash flows.

stories.headline: Japan advisers prioritise real-income growth
stories.body: Reuters reported that private-sector members of Japan's economic policy council urged sustained income and productivity gains rather than treating 2% inflation as the final objective. They said consumption remained weak and real-income improvements were not fully realised.
stories.analysis: Meeting an inflation target does not necessarily restore household purchasing power.
stories.watch_next: Real wages, consumption and BOJ decisions.
